question: What is the main goal of using digital health in midwifery practice?

options.A: To improve health services using information and communication technologies
options.B: To reduce the number of trained midwives working in rural areas
options.C: To completely replace physical clinics with virtual spaces
options.D: To eliminate the need for paper records entirely within twenty-four hours

explanation: Digital health uses technology tools to support and enhance healthcare delivery rather than abolish physical infrastructure. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why do student midwives in Nigeria need to learn about digital health tools?

options.A: Traditional clinical assessments are no longer taught in nursing schools
options.B: International agencies require every midwife to own a personal smartphone
options.C: Technology is increasingly integrated into maternal health tracking and communication
options.D: Paper documentation is now illegal across all Nigerian healthcare facilities

explanation: As digital tools become more common in healthcare, midwives must understand them to track trends and intervene timely. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which situation is a clear example of using telemedicine?

options.A: Distributing printed health pamphlets during a community immunization drive
options.B: Performing a routine surgical procedure inside a sterile operating theater
options.C: Providing healthcare services when distance separates the provider and client
options.D: Conducting an in-person physical pelvic examination at a local clinic

explanation: Telemedicine specifically bridges geographical distance by using electronic communication tools for care delivery. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is a major limitation of relying on telemedicine during pregnancy care?

options.A: It completely prevents midwives from giving dietary advice
options.B: It cannot replace hands-on physical assessments like abdominal palpation
options.C: It requires every pregnant woman to buy expensive computer hardware
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about their labor signs

explanation: Virtual consults cannot substitute for physical touch, such as checking fetal position or measuring fundal height. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h2)

question: What type of devices are mainly used for mobile health (mHealth) programs?

options.A: Paper appointment cards and physical filing cabinets
options.B: Heavy laboratory centrifuges and ultrasound machines
options.C: Wired desktop computers located only in teaching hospitals
options.D: Mobile phones and wireless monitoring gadgets

explanation: mHealth relies directly on portable wireless and mobile technology to deliver health information and services. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h3)

question: How do SMS appointment reminders help pregnant women in local communities?

options.A: They reduce missed antenatal care visits by prompting timely attendance
options.B: They automatically transport the patient to the clinic free of charge
options.C: They replace the need for professional labor and delivery attendants
options.D: They diagnose pregnancy complications before symptoms appear

explanation: Text message prompts help women remember their scheduled clinic dates, ensuring better continuity of care. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is a common feature of mHealth programs used in Nigeria?

options.A: Satellite tracking of every newborn child until adulthood
options.B: Mandatory virtual reality headsets for all pregnant teenagers
options.C: Automated robotic surgery performed via text message commands
options.D: Interactive voice response systems and SMS messaging for education

explanation: Voice messages and texts are widely used to share health education because mobile phones are so common. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h4)

question: A midwife uses a mobile phone to call an ambulance for a woman with postpartum hemorrhage. Which delay in the three delays model does this help reduce?

options.A: The delay in receiving adequate treatment after arriving at the hospital
options.B: The delay in reaching a health facility due to transport issues
options.C: The delay in purchasing prescribed medications from a pharmacy
options.D: The delay in deciding to seek medical care

explanation: Coordinating emergency transport via phone directly targets transit delays between rural clinics and referral hospitals. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is a major benefit of remote consultations for low-risk pregnant women?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any blood pressure checks throughout pregnancy
options.B: Allowing women to give birth safely at home without professional help
options.C: Guaranteeing a completely pain-free labor and delivery process
options.D: Reducing transportation costs and unnecessary hospital visits

explanation: Virtual check-ins save women the expense and effort of traveling for routine queries or minor issues. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h5)

question: How do remote monitoring tools help busy primary health clinics?

options.A: By preventing pregnant women from asking questions outside clinic hours
options.B: By replacing all trained midwives with automated computer software
options.C: By helping triage patients so high-risk conditions receive prompt attention
options.D: By shutting down clinics so staff can work entirely from home

explanation: Remote tracking helps sort client needs, allowing limited clinical resources to focus on high-risk cases. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to tele-midwifery in Nigeria?

options.A: Unreliable electricity supply in rural communities
options.B: High costs of mobile data for economically disadvantaged families
options.C: Excessive availability of free high-speed broadband in every village
options.D: Poor network coverage in remote geographic areas

explanation: Free high-speed broadband is not a reality in most rural areas; poor connectivity and high data costs are actual barriers. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why might some community members hesitate to use digital health consultations?

options.A: Mobile phones are medically proven to cause pregnancy complications
options.B: Government policies strictly forbid the use of mobile phones for health
options.C: Midwives refuse to answer phone calls after normal working hours
options.D: They prefer traditional face-to-face interactions for sensitive health issues

explanation: Cultural reliance on physical presence and personal touch often breeds skepticism toward virtual healthcare. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h6)

question: What must a midwife get from a client before sharing her health details on a digital platform?
explanation: Midwives are ethically required to get proper informed consent before transmitting any client health information digitally. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why is using unencrypted social media apps for patient consultations discouraged?

options.A: They lack adequate security to protect sensitive patient data from breaches
options.B: They prevent midwives from typing medical terminology correctly
options.C: They automatically delete all messages after five seconds
options.D: They charge extremely high subscription fees for healthcare workers

explanation: Standard social media chats are often unsecured, risking patient confidentiality and privacy violations. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h7)

question: What model of care best describes the future of midwifery practice with technology?

options.A: A hybrid model blending digital interventions with physical clinical care
options.B: A completely automated system with zero human midwives involved
options.C: An international relocation of all maternity care to virtual servers
options.D: A total return to paper records and in-person-only consultations

explanation: Technology will support and enhance traditional midwifery care rather than completely replace human practitioners. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h8)

question: What is needed to prepare student midwives for future technological changes in practice?

options.A: Replacing all clinical postings with online video gaming simulations
options.B: Embedding digital literacy directly into nursing and midwifery curricula
options.C: Requiring students to build their own smartphone applications from scratch
options.D: Restricting student access to computers until they graduate

explanation: Integrating digital health training into education prepares students to use upcoming tools safely and effectively. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h8)
